problem: Every timer tick appended another room poll to the same promise chain as heartbeat frames. Slow polls could accumulate ahead of a valid heartbeat and let presence expire while the socket remained open.
change: Keep at most one scheduled or in-flight poll per socket. Coalesce redundant ticks; reset the latch after success or failure. The next poll reads current source state and current private cursor.
evidence_scope: The production-handler regression uses service doubles and controlled timers; it proves queue behavior, not PostgreSQL or the sole historical cause of METHOD18. The first attempted fixture lacked app.route and is retained separately from the valid red counterexample.
compatibility: No database, wire, snapshot, policy or clock changes. Current source retains the action timing correction as a separate revision.
rollback: Previous image remains schema/policy compatible but retains both known timing and poll-backlog defects. Operational rollback quiesces private scopes and keeps new private starts disabled; functional compatibility testing is qualified separately.
